outcome: cognitive function (selective attention, multitasking abilities, reaction times)
cohort: The study involved postpartum women treated at Sergio Bernales Hospital, Peru, with data collected from 184 medical records and cognitive function assessed in 30 of these women.
finding: Several factors, including cesarean delivery and preterm gestational age, were strongly associated with postpartum anemia, and women with postpartum anemia showed significant long-term differences in reaction times and cognitive function nearly three years postpartum.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was strongly associated with an increased risk of postpartum anemia (OR = 3.320).
followup_time: nearly three years after birth (for cognitive assessment)
cross-section timing: Medical record data for risk factors was collected in 2022; cognitive function was assessed nearly three years postpartum.
gest_age: Gestational age was collected, with preterm gestational age identified as a risk factor for postpartum anemia.
